lede: Tuesday is the week's heaviest lift: a newly seated Town Council takes up second reading of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, which would write new landscaping and historic-review standards into Telluride's Land Use Code — that's a real vote with lasting consequences for how properties are built and maintained here. The same day, the Telluride Housing Authority considers a new primary-residency policy for dependents in split-custody households, and Thursday's Planning & Zoning session digs into the Carhenge redevelopment and other Town-owned projects in the Accommodations 2 zone.

notable.stake: Second-reading vote on wildfire code amending Land Use, landscaping, and historic-review rules.
New primary-residency policy for split-custody dependents could affect housing eligibility determinations.
Public review of Carhenge redevelopment subdivision and concept plans on Town-owned land.
